dossiers.title: Jagged Alliance 3
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Squad-based tactical engagements combine action points, flanking, overwatch, cover and deliberate ammunition use; players differ about how reliably these options are explained and balanced.
Named mercenaries have distinct specializations and personalities, with skill growth, perks, gear customization and party combinations influencing tactical options.
Beyond fights, managing squads across sectors, training militia, treating wounds, securing income and completing branching local quests make campaign planning an important second layer.
Veteran players highlight returning mercenary banter, music, character interactions and freedom of approach, while acknowledging the sequel simplifies familiar systems.
Enemy durability, armor, accuracy and equipment scaling receive conflicting reactions: some report satisfying tactical preparation, others feel individual shots lack impact.
Criticism includes limited control over synchronized squad moves, absent or confusing pre-combat pause behavior, and awkward interface or logistics compared with earlier Jagged Alliance games.
Some long-play accounts say a few powerful sniper or machine-gun setups reduce late-game variety and can make extended map-clearing routine; other players value experimentation.
Stealth is divisive: one player finds its detection and takedowns inconsistent, while a discussion explains how silent weapons and specialized perks make scouting and stealth viable.
Mission locations and encounters leave room for optional tactical approaches, though players disagree about whether restricted maps and strategic systems fully match earlier series entries.

dossiers.title: My Time at Sandrock
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players describe a builder's daily loop of commissions, scavenging, mining, crafting machine components and upgrading a workshop to fulfill orders.
Restoring a struggling desert town through main commissions and community projects offers a strongly guided long-form progression alongside optional gathering and social activities.
Characters, town relationships, humorous dialogue, romance and story arcs are repeatedly cited as major motivations to continue beyond efficient crafting.
Players split on the very long story: some enjoy relaxing routines over many dozens or hundreds of hours, while others find prolonged quest gating and slow waiting bloated.
New machines, mining and building recipes, crops and relationships gradually expand activities, though a player says upgrades can be exhausted well before the late main story ends.
Water scarcity, sandstorms, gathering loops and material bottlenecks define the desert setting; for some they add meaningful resource planning, for others they impede cozy flow.
The combat and routine gathering challenges are described as generally forgiving, with the main appeal lying in exploration, crafting and social progression rather than high combat mastery.
A multiplayer player says cooperative mode feels more like a separate builder sandbox than a shared version of the detailed single-player narrative, making mode expectations important.
Repetitive resource errands and story-trigger waiting can become draining after many hours, although other long-play users report enjoying relaxed daily workshop activities.
The warm cartoony presentation contrasts with an arid post-apocalyptic setting; players praise views, environmental storytelling and improving the settlement.

dossiers.title: Chicken Police - Paint it RED!
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players praise the sharply staged black-and-white animal noir aesthetic and detective atmosphere; both Russian and English first-hand accounts emphasize the unusual visual identity.
Voiced dialogue, music and the interplay of the central detective partners are recurring strengths, making the mystery feel more like a fully performed noir story.

Much of the interaction consists of examining places, gathering clues and choosing interview questions; a Russian player's account found the core loop enjoyable but lighter than a more demanding detective game.
Player completion reports cluster around a compact six-to-ten-hour narrative experience, with more time spent listening and reading than solving complex systems.
Interrogation scoring, dialogue options and occasional minigames supply modest challenge, but some players find the right choices unclear or mechanically shallow.
Some players complain about dialogue navigation and save or achievement conveniences, which can make rechecking story details and completion chores tedious.
The story moves through dialogue-heavy locations and interviews with animal inhabitants, emphasizing clue collection and escalating narrative revelations rather than broad free-roaming.
An older discussion reports a puzzle trigger that did not advance until reloading a save; the report establishes a past isolated problem, not the game's present technical condition.
Humor and eccentric anthropomorphic characters sit beside serious detective-noir tropes; the tonal blend is central to the game's identity.
The short linear mystery and simple minigames limit mechanical variety, while a player who replayed for achievements found additional completion relatively straightforward.
